summary: The `sir` resource pointed at /publications/State%20of%20Industry%20Reports/sir{year}.pdf, which is an HTTP 404 with a 9-byte body for EVERY year. The published form is .../State%20of%20Industry%20Report%20<year>.pdf. The command had therefore never worked. The same 404 also left a FALSE CLAIM in the shipped descriptions: "sir2023.pdf has NO usable text layer - 0 bytes extract", which was measured against the 9-byte 404 body, not against the report. That wording is corrected here too.
reason: Phase 5's live matrix caught it as the only failing command: 120 of 122 tests passed and both failures were `sir 2024` (happy_path and json_fidelity), each exiting 3 on an HTTP 404. PROBED DIRECTLY: sir2024.pdf and sir2023.pdf both return 404 with a 9-byte body, while State%20of%20Industry%20Report%202024.pdf returns 200 / 9,350,361 bytes and State%20of%20Industry%20Report%202023.pdf returns 200 / 3,425,763 bytes. The shipped `sources` catalogue had ALREADY measured the correct form and had ALREADY declared the mismatch as a gap with verdict upstream_bug, saying in as many words that correcting spec.yaml was a different patch it would not make. This is that patch. The wrong filename does not appear anywhere in the probe evidence, whose own line about NEPRA's index records the real 'State of Industry Report 2022.pdf' and 'State of Industry Report 2023.pdf' names — so it was introduced between research and spec authoring. A COLLATERAL CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE PATH FIX: the absorb manifest killed `sir --table` citing, among other things, 'sir2023.pdf extracts 0 bytes; no usable text layer'. That was measured against the 9-byte 404 page, not against a PDF. Measured against the REAL document on 11 Sep 2026 — 3,425,763 bytes, %PDF-1.6, 457 /Font references, 517 streams — decompressing the content streams yields 866 BT text blocks and 871,270 characters of extractable text. THE SIR PDFs HAVE A REAL TEXT LAYER. The `sir --table` kill still stands on its other grounds (610.6 MB across ten reports, 331 MB for SIR 2025 alone, and per-character kerning that makes exact string matching return false absences), but that one leg of the reasoning was false and the handoff's HARD NEGATIVE recording it has been corrected. SECOND DEFECT, same root cause: because every year 404'd, the 0-byte extraction was attributed to the REPORT rather than to the missing route, and that attribution was written into promoted_sir.go Short/Long, internal/mcp/tools.go, tools-manifest.json, spec.yaml, README.md, SKILL.md and the nepra_scope.go limit for circular debt. MEASURED AFTER THE PATH FIX: sir 2023 returns 3,425,763 bytes of application/pdf carrying 368 /Font objects, so the report plainly HAS a text layer. The build's own sources catalogue never agreed with the claim either - it records sir-2023 as text_layer "unmeasured", which is the correct statement of an absent measurement. A CLI whose cardinal rule is that absence is never zero must not ship a 0 it never observed.
reapply_after_regen: spec.yaml is FIXED, so a regen emits the correct path into resource_paths.go and promoted_sir.go without help. Re-check anyway, because the failure is silent in the worst way: the command exits 3 with a plausible 'resource not found', which is indistinguishable from a year NEPRA genuinely does not publish. TWO call sites in the generated internal/cli/promoted_sir.go carry the literal path — the `pp:path` annotation and the `path :=` assignment — and both must read State%20of%20Industry%20Report%20{year}.pdf. VERIFY WITH DATA: `sir 2024 --dry-run` must print GET .../State%20of%20Industry%20Report%202024.pdf, and `sir 2024 --json` must return bytes 9350361 with content_type application/pdf. internal/cli/sources.go's declared gap for this route was flipped from upstream_bug to fixed and carries the collateral text-layer correction; do not revert it to the old wording. A regen also restores the false text-layer sentence in promoted_sir.go, internal/mcp/tools.go, tools-manifest.json and spec.yaml, because it is carried in the spec description. Re-apply the corrected wording in all of them, and re-check that nepra_scope.go's circular-debt limit does not reacquire it.
validated_outcome: `sir 2024 --json` returns exit 0, content_type application/pdf, bytes 9,350,361 — matching the sources catalogue's independently measured figure exactly. `sir 2023` returns 3,425,763 bytes, likewise matching. Phase 5's live matrix goes from 120/122 to 122/122. The corrected route is the one the catalogue had measured all along, so no new claim is introduced: the fix makes the fetch path agree with the evidence already in the build. DESCRIPTION CORRECTION: all seven surfaces now say the command returns PDF bytes and that the reports are very large, and make NO text-layer claim; the circular-debt scope limit keeps its two TRUE grounds (610 MB across ten reports at 68-164 KB/s with SIR 2025 at 316 MB, and per-character kerning causing false absences) and drops the false one. No test pinned the old string. 16 packages green, gofmt and vet clean, live dogfood re-run after the edit.
upstream_issue: TO FILE - the spec's happy_args (year=2024) were exercised by no gate before Phase 5's live matrix, so a path that 404s on EVERY possible argument shipped through Phase 3's completion gate, all six shipcheck legs and the Sample Output Probe. The probe samples novel-feature examples only; `sir` is a promoted generated resource and has none. A generator-side or shipcheck-side liveness check of each resource's own happy_args would have caught it immediately.
